quote: Inflammatory monocytes respond rapidly to microbial stimuli by secreting cytokines and antimicrobial factors, express the CCR2 chemokine receptor, and traffic to sites of microbial infection in response to monocyte chemoattractant protein (MCP)-1 (CCL2) secretion.
summary: Review of monocyte defence against pathogens that describes CCL2-driven, CCR2-dependent monocyte trafficking to infected tissue, with no UC data.

quote: The stressor also increased circulating levels of IL-6 and MCP-1, which were significantly correlated with stressor-induced changes to three bacterial genera (i.e., Coprococcus, Pseudobutyrivibrio, and Dorea).
summary: Social stress in mice raised circulating MCP-1 and this depended on the microbiota; not a colitis model.

quote: Infection of monolayers of human colon epithelial cell lines (T84, HT29, Caco-2) with invasive strains of bacteria (Salmonella dublin, Shigella dysenteriae, Yersinia enterocolitica, Listeria monocytogenes, enteroinvasive Escherichia coli) resulted in the coordinate expression and upregulation of a specific array of four proinflammatory cytokines, IL-8, monocyte chemotactic protein-1, GM-CSF, and TNF alpha, as assessed by mRNA levels and cytokine secretion.
summary: Invasive bacteria and TNF or IL-1 upregulated MCP-1 mRNA and secretion in human colon epithelial cell lines and in freshly isolated colon epithelial cells.

quote: Finally, we demonstrate that the chemokine CCL2 contributes to microbiota-induced WAT inflammation in lard-fed mice.
summary: In diet-fed mice, CCL2 contributed to microbiota-induced adipose tissue inflammation; this is a metabolic model, not colitis.
Phase 1b trial of the CCR2 inhibitor PF-04136309 with FOLFIRINOX in pancreatic cancer; CCL2 appears only as part of the axis background.

quote: MCP-1 (Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1), also known as Chemokine (CC-motif) ligand 2 (CCL2), is from family of CC chemokines.
summary: General review of MCP-1/CCL2 function and its role in inflammatory diseases and COVID-19, with no UC-specific data.

quote: Accordingly, supernatants from activated neutrophils induced chemotaxis of Th17 cells, which was greatly suppressed by anti-CCL20 and anti-CCL2 antibodies.
summary: Activated neutrophils produced CCL2 and CCL20, and anti-CCL2 antibody blocked Th17 cell chemotaxis in vitro; Crohn disease gut tissue contained both cell types.

quote: Mechanistic analysis revealed that FAS-regulated monocyte chemotactic protein 1 (MCP-1) secretion by BMMSCs recruited T cells for FASL-mediated apoptosis.
summary: MSC-derived MCP-1 recruited T cells for FASL-mediated apoptosis in a mechanism that ameliorated DSS colitis, but MCP-1 itself was not directly perturbed.

quote: Cerebral recruitment of monocytes was abolished in inflamed mice that lacked MCP-1/CCL2 or CCR2.
summary: In mice with liver inflammation, loss of CCL2 abolished monocyte recruitment into the brain; not an intestinal model.

quote: Their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities are largely due to their abilities to scavenge the reactive oxygen species (ROS) and improvement of antioxidant status by attenuating the activity of NF-κB and suppressing the expression of several inflammatory cytokines and chemokines including monocyte chemotactic protein-1 (MCP-1), nitric oxide synthase, cyclooxygenases, lipoxygenases, cellular adhesion molecules, tumor necrosis factor and interleukins.
summary: Review of baicalin and baicalein anti-inflammatory effects; MCP-1 suppression is named only as one of many downstream effects.

quote: Mice lacking CCL2 or CCR2, but not CCL5 or CCR5, were protected against OA with a concomitant reduction in local monocyte/macrophage numbers in their joints.
summary: Ccl2-deficient mice and CCL2 synthesis inhibition were protected from osteoarthritis and joint monocyte infiltration, so CCL2 drives joint inflammation; not a gut model.

quote: Here, we discuss the significance of CCL2 (MCP-1), CCL7, CCL8, CCL11, CCL13, CCL14, CCL15, CCL16, CCL17, CCL22, CCL23, CCL24, and CCL26.
summary: Review of CC chemokines including CCL2 in tumour biology, with no colitis data.

quote: While classically it has been identified by increased cytokine or chemokine expression, such as increased MCP-1, RANTES, IL-6, interferon (IFN) gamma or TNFα, mechanistically, immune cell infiltration is a prominent feature of the dysfunctional AT.
summary: Review of adipose tissue immune cells that lists MCP-1 among raised cytokines with no specific result on it.

quote: Mice deficient of the chemokine receptor CCR2 or the ligand CCL2 failed to recruit Gr1(+) inflammatory monocytes, whereas dendritic cells and resident tissue macrophages remained unaltered.
summary: CCL2-deficient mice failed to recruit inflammatory monocytes to the ileum and developed intestinal necrosis and death after Toxoplasma infection, so CCL2 was protective.

quote: Deletion of CCL2 blocked progression from dysplasia to adenocarcinoma and reduced the number of colonic MDSCs in a spontaneous mouse model of colitis-associated CRC.
summary: CCL2 deletion or neutralisation reduced MDSC accumulation and tumour progression in colitis-associated colorectal cancer models, and CCL2 was raised in patient tumours.

quote: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) analyses indicated abundant production of three chemokines, i.e. monokine induced by interferon-gamma (MIG), interferon-inducible protein 10 (IP-10) and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), in the DSS-irritated intestine of WT but not of IFN-gamma(-/-) mice.
summary: MCP-1 was abundant in the inflamed intestine of DSS-treated wild-type mice but not IFN-gamma-deficient mice, so its production depends on IFN-gamma.

quote: We found supportive evidence for 21 out of 40 CD loci identified in a recent CD GWAS meta-analysis, including two loci which had only nominally achieved replication (rs4807569, 19p13; rs991804, CCL2/CCL7).
summary: A Crohn's disease GWAS gave supportive evidence for the CCL2/CCL7 locus (rs991804); this is Crohn's, not UC, and no direction is stated.

quote: Furthermore, interfering with TREM-1 engagement leads to the simultaneous reduction of production and secretion of a variety of pro-inflammatory mediators such as TNF, IL-6, IL-8 (CXCL8), MCP-1 (CCL2), and IL-1beta.
summary: TREM-1 blockade reduced a set of mediators including MCP-1; CCL2 is one of several readouts in a TREM-1 paper.

quote: Challenge of CaCO-2 cells with non-pathogenic E coli and Lactobacillus sakei induced expression of IL-8, MCP-1, IL-1beta, and TNF-alpha mRNA in the presence of underlying leucocytes.
summary: Non-pathogenic bacteria induced MCP-1 mRNA in Caco-2 cells co-cultured with leucocytes.

quote: Furthermore, SCFAs can specifically inhibit constitutive monocyte chemotactic protein-1 (MCP-1) production and LPS-induced interleukin-10 (IL-10) production in human monocytes without affecting the secretion of other cytokines and chemokines examined.
summary: Short-chain fatty acids lowered MCP-1 secretion by human monocytes; MCP-1 was a readout of SCFA treatment and was not itself perturbed.

quote: Some of the inflammatory signaling molecules involved in CKD include: monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), bradykinin B1 receptor (B1R), nuclear factor κB (NF-κB), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα), transforming growth factor β (TGF-β), and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF).
summary: Review of renal fibrosis signalling that lists MCP-1 among inflammatory mediators in kidney disease; no UC data.

quote: Preliminary data suggest a relationship between PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and objective response.
summary: In an anti-PD-1 cancer trial, tumour PD-L1 expression was associated with objective response; this is oncology with no UC data.
Phase 3 trial of nivolumab (anti-PD-1) in lung cancer; PD-L1 appears only as a subgroup stratifier.

quote: ConclusionsAntibody-mediated blockade of PD-L1 induced durable tumor regression (objective response rate of 6 to 17%) and prolonged stabilization of disease (rates of 12 to 41% at 24 weeks) in patients with advanced cancers, including non-small-cell lung cancer, melanoma, and renal-cell cancer.
summary: Anti-PD-L1 antibody gave durable tumour responses in advanced cancer patients; the outcome is oncologic and says nothing about colitis.
Trial of nivolumab and ipilimumab in melanoma; PD-L1 appears only as a tumour subgroup.
